verdicts.summary: The release path clears only the provider-thread roster. Active subagent, command and dynamic_tool turn items and subagent records stay running, and they also drive Waiting. A thread with a background subagent can therefore stay Waiting after release.
verdicts.scenario: 1. A Claude or Muse thread launches a background subagent (Agent with run_in_background). The roster lists it as kind subagent, and a `subagent` turn item stays running because the registry outlives the root turn (ClaudeAdapterV2.ts:3580-3584). 2. The root run settles. 3. The session is released by detach (archive/settle), manual close, or a CLI crash (`runtime_error`). 4. `writeReleasedBackgroundWorkEvents` (:850-880) rewrites only `pendingBackgroundTasks` and leaves status untouched. Nothing in the diff interrupts the running turn items or ends the subagent records. 5. `derivePendingBackgroundWork` takes work from the roster and also from `pendingBackgroundTurnItems`, which keeps any active `command_execution`, `dynamic_tool` or `subagent` item (orchestrationV2PendingBackgroundWork.ts:13-17, 193-202, 275-279). It is gated only on the latest run being settled and no active run. 6. The surviving running subagent item keeps the thread listed as Waiting (#15239) until a server restart. The sibling paths end those items explicitly: Orchestrator.ts:8480-8563 interrupts items and calls `endOrphanedNativeSubagent`, and ProviderRuntimeRecoveryService.ts:522-548 cancels subagents and runless root turns. I did not confirm that nothing else ends the subagent item after the CLI dies. Events from the dying adapter are not persisted once `failSubscribers` runs (:1081).
verdicts.consequence: For the common case of a background subagent, the bug the change targets is only partly fixed. The roster is empty, but the thread still shows Waiting and the stale pending-work list. Only a restart clears it, because that recovery cancels the items and subagents. Command-only rosters are fine, since the background launch item completes at launch (claude_background_task_interrupt/output.ts:42-49).

verdicts.summary: If the thread's projection disappears between the roster read and the write, the whole release record write may fail and be retried indefinitely, and the error also surfaces to the caller of detach, close or release.
verdicts.scenario: 1. A release captures a roster in `readReleasedBackgroundTasks`. Read failures are caught there (:1066, 483-489). 2. The thread is deleted before `writeReleasedBackgroundWorkEvents` runs. The write's `getThreadRecords` call (:852) is not wrapped in a catch, and Orchestrator.ts:8531 shows it can fail with ProjectionStoreThreadNotFoundError. 3. `writeReleaseRecords` joins the exit with `Exit.asVoidAll` (:910-913). The failure makes `recorded` a failure (:1100), so `retryReleaseRecords` re-runs it on an exponential schedule capped at 30s with no attempt limit (:943-951). Each retry also re-runs the session-stopped and request writes. I could not confirm that `getThreadRecords` fails for a deleted thread with the schema it reads, or how reachable the race is. ThreadDeletion's detach effect runs after the deletion commit, so the read phase usually fails first and returns [].
verdicts.consequence: Possibly a never-ending retry fiber that logs `provider-session-release-records-failed` every 30s, plus an error returned from the release call.
